acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE GRANT'S SCOPE READ: account-wide `s3:GetBucketNotification` on `*` beside the role's existing account-wide reads versus a 34-bucket enumeration -- which you chose, why, and the blast radius (the derive role only; no other principal moved). A reading act; NO verdict; graded by 3.0.0_SA_CVO at L9.
acceptance.invocation: iam get-role-policy over the role's inline documents + the item2a.tf AccountWideReadOnly statement read at c7b6a0d200 + the derive's own ListAllMyBuckets denominator; no single command decides it
acceptance.expect: a reading, recorded with no verdict
acceptance.output_evidence: CHOSE Resource "*", not a 34-bucket enumeration. THREE reasons, in order of weight. (1) THE ENUMERATION WOULD LAPSE SILENTLY. The bucket set is not a constant: the derive discovers it at run time with ListAllMyBuckets, and the day a 35th bucket is created the enumerated grant would read 34 and report unreadable=1 -- or, worse, the collector would swallow the AccessDenied exactly as it did before the C-3 fix. This is the same failure shape CLAUDE.md s.5 names for the cross-firm ban list ('an enumerated ban list lapses SILENTLY when a name changes') and the shape row W1-S7 closes on ('an account-wide read-only describe grant that enumerates its verbs will always lag the code that adds a new one'). An enumerated RESOURCE list lags the estate the same way an enumerated ACTION list lags the code. (2) IT MATCHES THE SCOPE ALREADY IN FORCE. The role's sibling reads -- GetBucketPolicy, GetBucketVersioning, GetBucketLocation, ListAllMyBuckets, and 60-odd describe/list verbs across ten services -- are all Resource "*" in the AccountWideReadOnly statement. GetBucketNotification is the same kind of verb: a per-bucket READ whose whole purpose is estate-wide inventory. Scoping this one action to a list while its siblings are account-wide would not reduce the role's reach by one byte; it would only make the role's grant harder to read. (3) THE ACTION IS READ-ONLY AND SINGULAR. GetBucketNotification returns a bucket's notification CONFIGURATION -- which events route to which Lambda, queue or topic. It reveals no object, no object data, no bucket contents; ListBucket (which the role already holds, scoped) is the enumerating verb, and PutBucketNotification is the mutating twin, measured implicitDeny on this principal in D12-AC2. BLAST RADIUS, measured not assumed: ONE principal moved. The apply's address list is one address; the apply summary is '1 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed'; the created id is opal-globgrph-derive-runner-task:DeriveRunnerBucketNotificationRead. No managed policy was attached, no bucket policy was touched, no other role or user appears in the plan. The role is assumable only by ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com and is used by the globgrph derive/producer task families. WHAT THE GRANT LETS AN ATTACKER DO IF THE TASK IS COMPROMISED: read the estate's S3 event wiring for 34 buckets -- i.e. learn which Lambda fires on which prefix. That is the same information the graph this role exists to build then serves to the estate, and it is strictly less than the GetBucketPolicy the role already holds, which returns the full principal-and-condition text of every bucket policy. THE ALTERNATIVE I DID NOT TAKE, stated so the CVO can weigh it: a 34-ARN Resource list would have bounded the grant to today's buckets and would have made a new bucket's notification config unreadable until someone edited terraform. That is a real, if small, containment gain, and it is the right choice for a WRITE action or for anything touching object data. For a read-only inventory verb on an inventory role, I judged the silent-lapse cost higher than the containment gain. NOTE the placement caveat, which is a separate axis from scope: the action landed in its own inline policy in iam.tf rather than inside AccountWideReadOnly, because item2a.tf is outside this order's <paths> (row W1-S9). That changes no permission -- IAM evaluates the union -- but it does mean a reader auditing the AccountWideReadOnly statement alone now sees one action fewer than the role holds.
acceptance.denominator: 1 principal moved of 1 named; 34 buckets reached of 34 the derive enumerates; 1 action added of 1 the order authorises
